record.original_question: For the same hook polynomial P_n(t) = Σ_{λ⊢n} ∏_{u∈λ} (h_u^2 + t)/h_u^2, is P_n(t) unimodal for every n?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.2(b) Each of the polynomials P_n(t) is unimodal.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a partition $\lambda = (\lambda_1 \ge \lambda_2 \ge \cdots)$ of a positive integer $n$ (written $\lambda \vdash n$), let the Young diagram of $\lambda$ be the set of cells $\{(i,j) : 1 \le j \le \lambda_i\}$. For a cell $u = (i,j)$ in this diagram, define the hook length
$$h_u = \lambda_i - j + \lambda'_j - i + 1,$$
where $\lambda'$ denotes the conjugate partition. Define the polynomial
$$P_n(t) = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} \prod_{u \in \lambda} \frac{h_u^2 + t}{h_u^2} \in \mathbb{Q}[t].$$

A polynomial $\sum_{k=0}^d a_k t^k$ with real coefficients is called unimodal if there exists an index $m$ such that $a_0 \le a_1 \le \cdots \le a_m \ge a_{m+1} \ge \cdots \ge a_d$.

Question: Is the polynomial $P_n(t)$ unimodal for every positive integer $n$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches on the unimodality of the hook polynomial $P_n(t) = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} \prod_{u} (h_u^2+t)/h_u^2$ did not return a definitive resolution of the conjecture. The polynomiality of related hook-content sums (Han–Stanley) is established, but no source confirming or refuting unimodality of $P_n(t)$ for all $n$ was found, so the status appears unknown to the searcher.

status_evidence.title: Stanley's work on unimodality (Brenti)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of Stanley's contributions to unimodality questions in combinatorics, including methods and open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Provides general context on unimodality conjectures, but does not record a resolution of the unimodality of P_n(t).

status_evidence.title: Some Combinatorial Properties of Hook Lengths, Contents, and Parts of Partitions (Stanley)
status_evidence.snippet: Stanley proves polynomiality results for symmetric functions of hook lengths over partitions of n, generalizing a conjecture of Han.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes polynomiality of related hook-content sums but does not address unimodality of the specific polynomial P_n(t).
